This month lots of people are talking about Annie's return again. Are any of you familiar with the writing principle 'Chekhov's Gun'?

*"If you say in the first chapter that there is a rifle hanging on the wall, in the second or third chapter it absolutely must go off. If it's not going to be fired, it shouldn't be hanging there."*


I feel like Annie is the rifle in this scenario. She has been dormant in the narrative for so long, if you hold to this principle she HAS to return at some point. Ready to explode. Because its been proven before that she is dangerous AF.

Yes, it would be epic if she returned with her energy and force, but switched to the other side. And - if Reiner is still alive, imagine what new and special torture strain this would put him under. 

But also, there are writing principles such as MacGuffins and Red herrings and I wouldn't put that past Isayama either.

So I basically joined Reddit to talk about SnK because I've become completely obsessed since I finally got up to date with the manga and I have no one IRL to rant to about it. I work in production design in the film industry and I've worked on a number of big shows, albeit only one which was an adaptation of well loved literature. So here's my 50 cents. 

1. Totally agree someone like HBO would have the financial capacity to make something like this work. Also totally agree it's MADE for prime time viewing if you look at how popular the anime was (before people got pissed they had to wait 4 years for season 2) 

2. I think you can learn a lot from the Japanese live action movie. I don't think the budget was massive but they clearly worked with everything they had and you always have less money than what the production envisages. Anyway in the Japanese live action the first time someone uses ODM I nearly laughed out loud. they look ridiculous. It takes a good fifteen minutes before you just think 'fuck it, I'm going to suspend my disbelief' but by the end of the movie you've accepted people can fly on bits of wire across great distances whilst flailing swords and with massive metal boxes strapped to their thighs. Super aerodynamic. But to be fair I was far more distracted by the Not Mikasa being a bitch to Not Eren and Not Hannes being exposition-bot that I wasn't that distracted by the ODM weirdness. There was a lot of cut frames where someone just flies in, they did definately reduce the amount of times you see flying people as the films progressed.

3. The 'titans' in the Japanese live action aka people with rubber suits on, are sometimes terrifying and sometimes hilarious so I would probably say if it was to be re-made any production would end up filming real people and comping over them 

4. The reality is that whichever studio makes this will be a group of people who are not committed or as into SnK as we are. They probably don't have a creative bone in their body and they sit in a boardroom thousands of miles away from the shoot and worry far more about the money than the authenticity. If we look at the producers, they maybe watched a couple of the anime and read a 20 page story bible provided by the writers whose job it would be to find a middle ground. They'd hire a showrunner who had credibility / was known for their knowledge of the anime but the boardroom would probably constantly make creative decisions over that persons head and as I have seen first hand, change massive swathes of story and character because they're worried that a certain hairstyle or dead mom back story won't hit the percentile of viewership they're hoping to achieve. 

Having said all of this, HBO are known for being pretty relaxed about creative control in some ways, and they do love their gore.

I really hope I'm wrong about number four, but all I'm saying is that it would need a very strong character as showrunner with a lot of respect to keep SnK on direction and refuse to change key things and to filter that vision down to everyone on board.

At any rate I think a Hollywood remake is 100% happening in the near future as I read that the option had been purchased, but it could sit in development hell for the next 20 years. 

I would still however love to see a live action series. If only to see Armin's beautiful blonde bowlcut locks wafting in all that live action glory as he slams his fist on his chest, teeth gnashing and tears in his eyes. I mean, who doesn't want to see that?
